tests.description: Reference: the VEGPARM/SOILPARM/GENPARM tables WRF loaded for the chem_opt = 170 idealized-column run (USGS land use, STAS soils), carried verbatim in the tbl_* fields of data/eqwefic/dumps/chem170_wrf/esm_dump_noah_601.json, for soiltyp = 4 (silt loam), vegtyp = 2 (dryland cropland and pasture) and slopetyp = 1. The four assertions that REDPRM itself produces -- smcmax, smcref, smcwlt, smcdry, plus nroot, rsmin and xlai -- are end-to-end: they compare against what SFLX returned, not against the table this component was built from. The remaining soil assertions are TRANSCRIPTION CHECKS against the same table, so they catch an off-by-one in the category index or a corrupted row but cannot catch a table that was wrong to begin with; the seven single-soil-type tests below are the independent check. shdmin = shdmax = 0 here, so the greenness selection takes the shdfac >= shdmax branch and xlai = laimax.

Reference: WRF 4.8 real-data run over the Colorado Rockies (8.1 km, 18 h, data/eqwefic/gwdo_real, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-gwdo), at a column whose soil category is 2 (loamy sand). smcmax, smcref, smcwlt and smcdry are REDPRM's own outputs for that column, dumped by WRF, so this is an INDEPENDENT end-to-end check of the SOILPARM lookup -- a different run, a different executable and a different land-use table from the one the component's table was taken from. Only soil quantities are asserted: that run uses the 20-category MODIS vegetation table (isurban = 13), not the USGS table this component carries, so its vegtyp indexes a different table and its vegetation parameters are deliberately NOT compared. Values are real32 from a single-precision WRF build, hence rel 1e-7 rather than the 1e-12 used against the kernel replay.
